# Effective Claude Code Usage

> A Quarto RevealJS presentation by Indrajeet Patil with practical advice for getting reliable work out of Claude Code.

The talk is organised around the four reasons a Claude Code session usually goes wrong, and the fix for each: tell Claude what it can't see, give it a check to run, enforce the rules that can't have exceptions, and change a default only when it costs too much. It then covers steering a session (Esc, rewind, `/clear`), unattended runs with `claude -p` and Git worktrees, and advice that current models have made unnecessary.

Reviewed against Claude Code v2.1.330 on 22 November 2026. Command availability depends on the installed version and configuration.

## Primary URL

- [Slides](https://www.indrapatil.com/effective-claude-code-usage/)

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/effective-claude-code-usage/)

## Topics

- Diagnosing why a Claude Code session went wrong
- What belongs in CLAUDE.md, path-scoped rules, skills, and MCP
- Specific prompts, and interview-driven specs
- Pass/fail checks, `/goal`, Stop hooks, and independent review
- Guidance versus enforcement: hooks, deny rules, sandbox, and managed settings
- Permission modes, effort levels, subagent cost, and context cost
- Steering with Esc, rewind, and `/clear`
- Unattended runs with `claude -p` and parallel sessions in Git worktrees
- Outdated advice to stop following
